reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: The picture doesn't feel like an absolute failure or even a cheat. It's more like a movie with too many ideas that hasn't quite figured out how to pull them all together.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Boldly creative in the style of Wes Anderson but with his own satirical quirks, Waititi's Jojo Rabbit is among 2019's best films.
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is told in a way that could only be done by Taika Waititi, and has become one of the most misunderstood films of the year.
reviews.author: Karen M. Peterson

reviews.text: Edgy and intriguing, reminding younger generations what happened more than 70 years ago.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Ultimately Jojo is a film about change: the possibility and process of it; how it happens; why it's compelling to watch.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: Drawing on his own experiences with prejudice growing up Jewish, writer-director Waititi makes a powerful and humorous satire of Nazi culture, a statement against hate, and a look at the absurdity of violence.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: One of the best films of the year, Jojo Rabbit nimbly zips through the full gamut of emotions: It's by turns uproarious, warm, heart-rending, horrifying, silly, surreal, scary and joyous.
reviews.author: Brandy McDonnell

reviews.text: The New Zealand director somehow, inexplicably, keeps hitting the right notes to make his peculiar composition work
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Taika Waititi has somehow managed to make a dark comedy with Hitler as one of the lead characters that's thought-provoking and hugely entertaining. It's also irresistible in all its weirdness.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: The comedy is blackened in just the right ways to make this a delicious satirical comedy. I was greatly entertained. (Full Content Review for Parents - Violence, Profanity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Davis probably faces the toughest challenge on screen, and he skillfully navigates the film's blend of melancholy and whimsy.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: It's a good joke for a while, but after two hours it felt like beating a dead unicorn.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: This is Waititi's main line of critique: Nazism as a kind of especially pernicious stan culture, its infantile practitioners the original teenyboppers.
reviews.author: Nadine Smith

reviews.text: Beneath the madcap action, the goony characters and Wes Anderson scenery beats a big heart coursing with the stuff of life, against all odds and, often, in the throes of unspeakable crimes.
reviews.author: Rick Levin

reviews.text: ...feels like a zany prank being pulled on a dictatorial teacher by the smartest kid in the room.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: It's the sort of failure worth saluting, ambitious, somewhat insane, aiming at a worthy target.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: An incredible feat of highwire artistry that results in a rare emotionally - and cinematically - complete film.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: This could've been something truly special if Waititi didn't insist on spending the majority of his time winking at the audience.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: It's one of the best films of the year and might just be the funniest.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: Just when you think cinema is getting routine, something like Jojo Rabbit hops along and perks it right back up, reminding us that, indeed, the medium is very often the message.
reviews.author: Randy Shulman

reviews.text: It's an uneasy balance between Jojo Rabbit's "Look at these idiots" mentality and the film's more conventional "Learn to love each other" arc.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: The film is wonderfully weird and irresistibly askew, punctuated by hilarity, tragedy and even anachronistic music.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is director Taika Waititi's first "blank check" movie, which would make you think that he'd push the boundaries as far as they could go. In actuality, he stays within his borders.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Making fun of Nazis might seem like an obvious joke, but Jojo Rabbit effectively brings both heart and darkness to the reality of Nazi Germany during World War II.
reviews.author: Katey Stoetzel

reviews.text: All the kids are great, though, and there are plenty of quirky bits.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: The acting is universally spectacular, both Davis and especially McKenzie making an indelible impression.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: "Jojo Rabbit" has many surprises in store for moviegoers ready to ride along with [Taika] Waititi's strikingly original screenplay.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: "Jojo Rabbit" is a smart, accessible, inclusive film that opens doors at a time when many are slamming them shut. It's a celebration of the gift of life that's inviting you to dance with it. So dance with it.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: To be sure, a chunk of people will never see Jojo Rabbit. A comedy about an adorable Nazi is kind of a big lift for some viewers. I get that and ask you to push past it anyway.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: The end result is both deliriously funny and unexpectedly poignant, as the film hovers between outright satire and timely lesson on tolerance.
reviews.author: Josh Davis

reviews.text: The ingredients are appetizing but the final mixture curdles.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Much purposely leans toward the absurd for sure, but it's definitely no laugh-a-minute romp, especially if you simply refuse to giggle at Hitler, et al.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Yet again, Taika Waititi does the impossible, and succeeds in bringing a quirky idea that really shouldn't work to the big screen.
reviews.author: Lana Stanczak

reviews.text: It's still ultimately defined by [Taika] Waititi's absurdist humor, but it's also surprisingly moving.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: JoJo's mother, a superb Scarlett Johansson, navigates a delicate balance.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Every strong point of Jojo Rabbit -- it's playful, pleasant, easy to watch -- creates equal and opposite distraction.
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: It's a little uneven in places, but the audacity at play here makes it easy for me to overlook some flaws, especially when the unexpected sweetness comes in.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: A wild and whimsical look inside a young Nazi boy's brain with Adolf Hitler as his imaginary friend. Bold and beautiful.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: JoJo Rabbit offers a creative satire with humor and humanity, about a German boy discovering what lies Nazi grown-ups told, in the unique, entertaining and moving style of director/writer Waititi.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is an emotive, feel-good satire that entangles heart and humanity, even if it may strife on packing in intensity.
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: This is a deeply, distressingly insulated picture. It's the Funko Pop Collector's Edition of 'Shoah'.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: By filtering anti-Semitism, racism, and bigotry through the lens of a child coming of age in Nazi Germany, Jojo Rabbit becomes a stirring takedown of the very concept of prejudice itself.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: There's a deep and sincere sweetness in the work of writer-director Taika Waititi. It's a kind of relentless and innocent good cheer that persists in the face of horror - to the point where the horror is obscured, or maybe defanged.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: It isn't every day you find yourself saying this about a movie, but I'll go there: Not enough Hitler.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: A perfect balance between powerful drama & laugh-out-loud comedy entwined in a coming of age movie about Nazis, WWII, a Jewish stowaway & the fragility of the human condition.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is effective at doing what Waititi presumably set out to do: make people think critically about what it is that informs our beliefs. And, you know, laugh while we do it.
reviews.author: Gabriella Geisinger

reviews.text: Yes, viewers will have divergent opinions on the propriety of this project. To be sure, though, it's funny, smart and sometimes moving.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: In spite of the film's unconventional and off-the-wall style, it isn't hard to see where the different dynamics of "Jojo Rabbit's" principal characters are headed. But the journey is delightful, heartbreaking and truly remarkable.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: An admittedly bizarre picture that...will offend some, [but] makes up in sheer energy and inventiveness what it lacks in tonal consistency.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: There's more to the complicated Jojo Rabbit than first appears, and only a director as committed, inventive, and life-affirmingly good-hearted as Waititi would even have a chance of pulling it off. He does, to unforgettable effect.
reviews.author: Erik Henriksen

reviews.text: There is no way this film should work. But it does, and it's brilliant in introducing groan-worthy puns and quips that soften you up before the genuine blows that come later.
reviews.author: Maria Sciullo

reviews.text: [An] elegantly turned if sometimes episodic comedy.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: If there's one person able to master the hacky sack dance of tonality such material demands, it's Waititi, who scores laughs with "Jojo Rabbit," but also respects the sobering reality of wartime loss.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Director Taika Waititi tries his hardest to find the funny in fascism. Mostly, he fails miserably.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: Waititi takes the old line that "history doesn't repeat itself but it often rhymes," and suggests that sometimes history is a profane limerick.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: It has ended up being one of the funniest, slyest, and most unexpectedly humane films of the year.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Waititi manages to walk the fine line between fantasy and drama, humor and wartime horror without losing his balance.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: ...it's able to tug at the heartstrings while simultaneously finding humor during one of the worst man-made catastrophes in human history.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: If the content of a film expressly about Nazi Germany can't fully reckon with its grave sins, maybe it was a bad idea from the start.
reviews.author: Josh Martin

reviews.text: Taika Waititi shows a very deft hand, both as a writer and a director...A hilarious movie, one of my favorites of the year so far.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: [It] ultimately finds itself growing very heavy while approaching its climax. Waititi does well to make certain this shift [from irreverence] doesn't arrive out of nowhere.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Gusto meets gravitas in one of the most oddly poetic and beautifully brazen movies you may ever see.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: It's such a lovely, moving, funny, different, original film with a fantastic script
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Leave it to Taika Waititi to portray Hilter as hilarious in this brilliant, colorfully off-color satire.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: This story is absolutely beautiful and poignant, while still managing to be quite funny. Juggling such varying emotions can sometimes be a struggle, but Taika Waititi is always up to the challenge.
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: After seeing a screening of director-screenwriter Taika Waititi's film I fear my brain put it in the context of today's hate-fueled climate here in America, and I woke up terrified. Again and again and again.
reviews.author: Chuck Yarborough

reviews.text: For all its creative efforts, JoJo Rabbit can seem a bit trivial.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Blazingly and brilliantly over the top, Jojo Rabbit's total dismissal of subtlety is its most ferocious ally and, only occasionally, its most frustrating foe in the war against hate.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: In the end, it's as surprisingly moving as it is challenging at times.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: [T]here is tremendous precedent for this kind of satire, and one of the most incredible things about Jojo Rabbit is that rather than wilting in the shadow of the greats, Taika Waititi has crafted a film worthy of the legacy.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit has an aesthetic that refers to Wes Anderson's cinema, but with greater content and ambitions. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: María Fernanda Mugica

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit draws upon the past to make salient points about the state of the world today, with Waititi urging us (sometimes in not so subtle ways) to pay attention to history...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: It works beautifully, each moment bursting with playfulness (and impeccable timing), and yet never losing sight of kindness.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: This is how ignorance might be overcome, the film posits - not right away but gradually over time, relationship by relationship.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: Humor can be a powerful weapon against hatred, and Jojo Rabbit is a master class in how it works.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Don't go into "Jojo Rabbit" expecting a side splitting comedy à la Mel Brooks. Waititi's film is a gentler thing and Scarlett Johansson's performance embodies his message.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: When Jojo Rabbit works, which is seldom, it functions in a way that still makes most of its core creative decisions seem questionable.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Whatever expectations I had before watching "Jojo Rabbit," they are nowhere near what Waititi and his cast and crew have accomplished in this fresh, funny and sad story about a boy and his mom.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: When people wondered if it could balance the lighthearted tone with the war...well, it manages that. A lot of that is done because we see it through the eyes of Jojo.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: As touching and sweet as this movie is, you never lose that overall sense of menace.
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: Taika successfully pulls off a tightrope walk from the top of the 368-meter Fernsehturm Berlin to the tallest point of the 331-meter Europaturm.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: As history, it's trite, and as a fairy tale about intolerance, it's an evergreen. As a commentary on current events and our balkanized tribalism, it's clearly applicable and more than a little prescient.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: [A]nachronisms...drive home the point that the past is present, and those who cannot laugh at the absurdity inherent in our world's history of hate are perhaps doomed to repeat it.
reviews.author: Rain Jokinen

reviews.text: "Jojo Rabbit" delivers a palpable human story that touches as we laugh and the world around explodes.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: People of compassion should seek out art offered from the perspective of those who can see the dangers of bigotry and hate because they've felt it first-hand. Also: Jojo Rabbit is an inventive, heartfelt, heartbreaking, very funny film.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is deeply flawed, the narrative sags too often through its 108 minutes, but in its final forty-five Waititi discovers a deeply endearing relationship that makes the whole journey worth it.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit thrives as both an intrepid satire and a sincere coming of age dramedy, seamlessly blending wacky humor with genuine heartbreak.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: It is morally facile to assume that there is an innocent, warm-hearted kid under every youth-sized Nazi uniform.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: JoJo Rabbit" does portray the Nazis in a heightened, satiric, silly manner, but this is not an insensitive or superficial film. By the end it packs a wallop.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit shines with its combination of understated laughs and, sometimes haunting, visual flourishes.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: [A] largely unremarkable movie that trafficks in sentimentality and a Pollyannaish worldview...
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: This is one subversively funny, sarcastic and unnerving satirical comedy trip into Nazi War-Time Germany. Writer/Director Taika Waititi (Thor: Ragnarok), a self-described Polynesian Jew, walks an artistic tightrope in this venture.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Laughing at the Nazis seems to be Waititi's only moral imperative with this movie, which becomes a pretty significant problem for it.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: It's Waititi's ability to balance unassailably goofy moments with an acknowledgment of real-life horrors that makes the movie exceptional.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Feels safe. And a little smug. ... And yet, it's an enjoyable, funny movie for most of its 108 minutes.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: An existing affection for Waititi's specific brand of humour will help audiences embrace this film, but the bold optimism of his worldview comes through in any context.
reviews.author: Dominic Corry

reviews.text: A beautifully crafted film, one that that, for much of its running time, maintains a measure of lightness and sweetness without flinching from the ugliness at the center of the story.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Taika Waititi's Third Reich romp is black comedy at its finest.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: Certainly, scholarly discussions are not the place for chuckles... But movies give us a safe space to mock what we would otherwise fight. And Jojo Rabbit is a remarkably funny tale.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: While his Nazi satire doesn't always strike a perfect balance, the humor and sentimentality he brings feels like something we could all use more of right about now.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Unfunny comedy rubs shoulders with unearned sentiment.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: A sprightly, attractively composed coming-of-age comedy set in World War II Germany, "Jojo Rabbit" is an audacious high-wire act.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Too soon? That's the question at the heart of whether you'll find "JoJo Rabbit" a story of acceptance and inclusion or an offensive lark. I'm in the former camp. Your mileage may vary.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: As a director, Waititi is in command of the movie's disparate elements and harmonizes them into a coherent whole.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: If "Jojo Rabbit" doesn't finally hold together as we'd like it to, it has attempted so much and been so completely its own film that begrudging it good wishes feels not really fair.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: Today, making fun of Hitler and his minions is both easy and pointless, because he poses no threat; Waititi is kicking a dead bull.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: "A movie like Blazing Saddles could never get made today", people incorrectly spout; you have one right here, and it's taking down Nazis and neo-Nazis alike. And it's a gem
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The film's ambition is admirable, and it's hard to imagine anyone more capable of wringing so many laughs from such a peculiar premise.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: A bold, ridiculous and controversial comedy.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit proves to be perhaps one of the most essential political films of the past five years, cutting through a complexity of issues with humor and pathos
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: Irony may not be dead, but the brand peddled by Jojo Rabbit is certainly DOA.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Perhaps it's the ease of Jojo Rabbit that made it an enervating viewing experience. Waititi's ability to engineer emotional effects is real, but it also verges on the mechanical...
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: It's such a fine line that this movie walks, and [director Taika Waititi] pulls off these incredible tonal swings. Like, they're acrobatic.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: It goes from the absurd to the poignant in a very acute way... It is so unique, so original, and such a refreshing breath of incredibly fresh air.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: An incisive, empathetic, intimate portrait of isolation. It's graceful, sweet and strange, and despite its twee exterior, it manages to stare social malaise right in the eye, giving it the kind of dressing-down that doesn't simply preach to the choir.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Waititi has been interested in likeable, sheepish misfits, and the hero of "Jojo Rabbit" is absolutely cut from this cloth.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: Waititi brings his signature wit to the script, and his direction walks a thin line that maintains the film's lighter tone while keeping the gravity of the whole Nazi Germany situation in check.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: You will find yourself alternately laughing and crying, but continuously dazzled, by Waititi's gorgeous, vaguely Wes Anderson-esque style.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Despite its setting in Nazi Germany, Taika Waititi's movie never risks actually disturbing its audience.
reviews.author: John Semley

reviews.text: [Jojo Rabbit] is a type of movie that's hard to pull off if you're the wrong director or writer for it. But luckily, Taika is behind it.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: It's a well-meaning idea that never quite succeeds on the levels of either comedy or drama. Call it a noble failure.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: Uneven but amusing WWII satire has violence, hate speech.
reviews.author: Joyce Slaton

reviews.text: This movie is deceptively-flippant, as there is so much more than meets the eye. A brilliant balancing act of tragedy & comedy. Despite how audacious Taika's Hitler role is, he's able to make us focus on what matters-JoJo's journey in overcoming hatred.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Shamefully, now is not a bad time to be a Nazi. But rather than explore the set up, Jojo Rabbit rushes ahead, once again, to the punchline.
reviews.author: Jeva Lange

reviews.text: An awkward, uneven film, with writer-director Taika Waititi conjuring some touching moments, but unable to pull off the magic act this "Rabbit" trick requires.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Waititi is trying to strike an impossible balance here, and while he wins a few big battles, he ends up losing the war.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: There is genuine zest in the unease of "Jojo Rabbit," and it's weirdly convincing as a portrait of childhood under surreal strain.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: The film doesn't lack for audacity, or ultimate purpose -- it's against hate and in favor of love. But the adaptation isn't funny enough to sustain the style, which owes an overt debt to Mel Brooks and amounts to Springtime for Hitler Youth.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Waititi's film is hilarious and heartbreaking - a testament to the fact that the children who get caught up in these terrible events are still kids.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: The film's certainty of its audacity only serves to underline its conceptual tepidness...
reviews.author: Chris Feil

reviews.text: Director Taika Waititi's self-described "anti-hate satire" blossoms into a big-hearted black comedy with the thorniest possible subject at its center.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is gently comic for a while, and then surprisingly affecting at the end, so perhaps it's not fair to wish that Waititi had opted to deal more directly with the horrors of the Third Reich.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: Visually brilliant, but fundamentally flawed in its logic. Also cheats by setting the film at the end of WW2, and treats Nazis as a "fad". Stephen Merchant has the best scene.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Taika Waititi's Nazi Satire Packs A Powerful Punch And Does It With Laughs.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: It risks going wrong in a dozen different ways and manages to avoid at least half of them.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: If only it had leaned into its inspired weirdness instead of trying to soften it into a schmaltzy dramedy, this could've been something great.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: As much as it makes you laugh, Waititi's must-watch effort is a warm hug of a movie that just so happens to have a lot of important things to say.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is just as emotionally investing and politically relevant as it is funny, making it a wholly unique and important landmark film.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbitcovers the expanse of emotions one would expect to find in a dramatic film about Germany in the waning days of World War II. It's a dazzling achievement from a supremely talented artist who wrote, directed and costars in the film.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: JOJO RABBIT is an immensely entertaining movie that is at once funny, poignant and memorable.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: As we all know, a solid performance by a child actor can make a film, just as a poor one will sink it. But young Davis is certainly up to the task, in fact he seems mature way beyond his years.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: It's funny, poignant, and unfortunately, more relevant than ever.
reviews.author: Anne Cohen

reviews.text: Taika Waititi is a triple threat genius taking on prejudice vs humanity in the guise of Adolf Hitler is a thought-provoking emotionally wraught film that hits all the notes with perfection via Monty Python - Mel Brooks comedic satire
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Waititi injects enough heart and wit into this enterprise to make a case that artists like him should at least be trying to find creative ways to educate new generations about the horrors of the past.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: You'll laugh, you'll cry - sometimes at the same time. But love or hate Jojo Rabbit, Taika Waititi's hit-and-miss Nazi dramedy is damn near impossible to shake. Our suggestion: Stick with Waititi, he's worth following anywhere.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Has just about everything you look for in a funny movie: a fresh idea, swagger, a strong point of view, and gifted comic actors such as Sam Rockwell and Rebel Wilson. One element it's missing, however, is that it isn't funny.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Waititi's simplistic view of human behavior and political history isn't even as sophisticated as Indiana Jones's witty cultural summation: "Nazis -- I hate those guys!"
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Silliness aside, Jojo Rabbit is about a ten-year-old boy who is forced to become an adult quickly. The moment he does, the film becomes a strong punch in the gut.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: Watiti's "Jojo Rabbit" puts a spotlight directly into the eyes of evil, as well as ridiculing hateful ideologies and dialogues contaminating today's world.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is a real joy of a film.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Taika Waititi mixes some dark moments with subversive comedy in "Jojo Rabbit," and if it's not on the level of Mel Brooks, it still stands out in a majorly compelling way.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Waititi's silly, irreverent performance takes the pomp and vigor out of the blustering Fuhrer, declawing the towering 20th century figure of hate. However, in doing so, he declaws his own satire, too.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Jojo [is] such an adorable creation, perfectly embodied by Davis, who exudes so much child-actor charm.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: Occasionally it misses the spot but on the whole this is a bitingly funny film, its satire and slapstick blunt and bold.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: A bold, original, often hilarious satire at the expense of Nazi Germany.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: Sorry, Taika, but you're no Mel Brooks.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit may not bring the bite of [Taika] Waititi's finest projects, but its heart is golden.
reviews.author: Carmen Paddock

reviews.text: Setting an anti-hate satire from the perspective of a 10-year-old in Nazi Germany sounds like a questionable task but Waititi & co. nail it.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: A hilarious, moving and timely dark comedy that ridicules and denounces hateful ideologies. Waititi has crafted one of the best films of 2019. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Taika Waititi's... ability to ridicule the Third Reich with a coming-of-age comedy mostly works by filtering its horrors through the prism of its pre-teen Hitler Youth protagonist.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The film is solidly well-made, with a terrific cast of comical geniuses romping through the scenery. So while the mood change from wacky to serious feels abrupt, the central story's pathos strikes a chord.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: There won't be a more important movie this year.
reviews.author: Sarah Manvel

reviews.text: Combined with larger-than-life characters, splintering tragedy, and a unique coming-of-age journey Jojo Rabbit conveys a message about love's ability to conquer loneliness, and that's a message that's fervently needed.
reviews.author: Joelle Monique

reviews.text: Even with its robust cast, and Waititi's way with both verbal humor and sight gags, the movie as a whole seems oddly evanescent.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: Overall, Jojo Rabbit is uneven at times but ultimately offers sweetness, comedy and an idiotically hilarious Hitler.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is a touching film about human compassion with an intimacy that is absolutely unparalleled. This is one of the most heartfelt and imaginative fairy tales of the year.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: The story, if not the entire film, is indeed great.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Its biting satire and message against the illogical and hateful messages depicted ensure that many will be sold on how the beloved Jewish director from New Zealand brings Nazi Germany to life.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: Waititi's riposte seems to be that, actually, it is vital that we laugh at Nazis - and Jojo Rabbit ensures that we do just that.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: Yeah, this is a tricky one. Lampooning the Nazis is a risky proposition, requiring a knife-edge balance between humor and horror.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: Despite the subject's supreme candidacy for mockery, it somehow fails to land a single meaningful hit.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: For some, the subject should be no laughing matter, but Waititi ridicules Nazi ideology with aplomb and his brand of winningly juvenile humour underpinned by sweetness is an ideal fit for a child's-eye view of events.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit features satire throughout the script that failed to make me laugh consistently.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: If you can take some rough chuckles, it's a wonderfully spirited and deeply humane story that revels in ridiculing antisemitism and small-mindedness.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: A few minutes in, and you're already choking on your giggles.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: With the world being what it is, maybe we need an act of radically cutesy sweetness such as this, and maybe JOJO RABBIT is a needed film. But there's also no denying this is more sugar than it is nourishment.
reviews.author: Johnny Donaldson

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit appeals to the best in all of us, and gives me hope that we can overcome our own struggles and just find a way to be good to one another.
reviews.author: J Hurtado

reviews.text: It's a coming of age story unlike any other, filled with the director's trademark heart and a soul-stirring argument against the ever ready darkness of unswerving, "patriotic" nationalism.
reviews.author: Marc Savlov

reviews.text: This generation's definitive political satire starring an imaginary Hitler.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: A fine film in a craftsmanly sense, but as a satire, it lacks bite.
reviews.author: Meg Shields

reviews.text: A bold and ambitious dramedy about the absurdity of hate. It worked better for me as a comedy than as a drama.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: There's a nagging feeling that Jojo Rabbit is giving us the kid-gloves version of the story.
reviews.author: Audra Schroeder

reviews.text: With such potential behind and on camera, it's hard not to be disappointed, but at the very least, Taiki Waititi has found a way to make a fun, hilarious movie about Nazi Germany, and that's got to count for something.
reviews.author: Justin Jones

reviews.text: It'll make you smile, it'll make you sad, and it'll make you believe in the best of us.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit feels like a necessary, warm-hearted mess, and it's well-worth your time to take a chance on it.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is a movie with a lot of heart, a lot of qualities that are sure to make it a hit with crowds, and just enough unique magic to make it one of the more pleasurable movie-going experiences of the year.
reviews.author: Lindsey Romain

reviews.text: Waititi's award-winning adaptation of Christine Leunens' novel Caging Skies is by turns hilarious, horrifying and ultimately heartbreaking.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: 'Jojo Rabbit' has so much positivity in its narrative that it could warm the iciest of hearts. It's absolutely lovely, and one of the year's very best films.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: A darkly whimsical satire, JoJo Rabbit [..] delivers a timely message about humanity and the very real danger of prejudices left unchecked.
reviews.author: Kimberley Elizabeth

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit makes the case that no one is ever too far lost in their fanatical devotion to a tyrannical leader to be reached by reason.
reviews.author: Marshall Shaffer

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit shows us that kindness and empathy can be revolutionary acts, and Taika Waititi shouts it from the rooftops for all to hear.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: "Jojo Rabbit" is uncomfortable in ways that work and ways that don't, but its heart is assured.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit tells a story that's both pointedly contemporaneous and fundamentally timeless...
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: JoJo Rabbit will wrap you up in the cinematic group hug that laughing and crying together in a dark theatre can bring.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: A pacifist movie that is much more mature than other attempts, such as the famous 'Life is Beautiful'. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Waititi's critique of the normalization of hate and the destruction of innocence is hardly subtext, and that Jojo Rabbit renders this palatable in a multiplex-friendly popcorn movie at this particular moment is nothing less than masterful.
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: Taika Waititi's Jojo Rabbit skillfully walks a tightrope that few films can. It is both a hilarious World War II satire and a deeply moving coming-of-age drama.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: Smugly tells us that the answer to counter Nazi hate is through love.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Waititi maintains his signature sweetness and zany brand of humor, making punch lines of Nazis and an unlikely hero of another "bad egg."
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Despite Jojo Rabbit's status as a satire, there are real emotional gut punches along the way, moments that Waititi calibrates as deftly as he does the more comedic elements.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is a bold and audacious comedy that everyone besides Nazis can enjoy.
reviews.author: Brent Goldman

reviews.text: Might not be Waititi's strongest, but this vibrant and entertaining comedy ends up being both an enjoyable time and a great breakthrough performance by Roman Griffin Davis.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Waititi wanted to light a bonfire but, at best, what we get is a sputtering candle.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: One of the sweetest and more delightful films of 2019, this zany satire had me grinning from ear to war. Hail, indeed.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: This is a dark satire that finds a way to make a case for understanding. As circumstances slowly chip away at Jojo's hate-driven worldview, the black comedy finds room for some genuinely touching moments.
reviews.author: Steve Pond

reviews.text: A brief and charming manual for satire. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: If it wasn't quite as astonishing as it was trying to be, it was at least audacious
reviews.author: Jay Stone

reviews.text: Strikes just the right balance between comedy, tragedy, and drama, the result being a very funny WWII film that nevertheless carries an incredibly important message about the here and now.
reviews.author: Chris Tilly

reviews.text: Taika Waititi has a knack for getting genuinely funny performances from child actors and with his latest film, Nazi satire Jojo Rabbit, he succeeds once again
reviews.author: Caitlin Quinlan

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit feels like next-level Taika Waititi. The concept needed spot-on work in every single department - it's all there and it comes together beautifully. Lots of laughs with purpose that send you on your way with hope in your heart.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Taika Waititi uses shock value and controversy to tell an ironically sweet story. It's up to each viewer to decide if the ends justify the means.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: True satire challenges and provokes. This one offers free hugs.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: There are laughs in the gap between Jojo's self-image and the reality... Jojo Rabbit could use more of that dynamic, and more of Waititi's subversive voice and willingness to upend cinematic norms.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: Taika Waititi goes well past the obvious hook of Funny Hitler by delivering a surprisingly emotional and hilarious look at how two children lean on one another to maintain their humanity.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: An "anti-hate satire" about an imaginary Hitler may seem a long, strange way to go about making this point - but it gets there in the end, with room for some deeply entertaining detours along the way.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: It may sound terrible, and it flirts with bad taste...Yet there's a sweetness that's quite extraordinary.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: ...when a film that's supposed to be a satire can't gain any of its best laughs at the expense of its stated target, that film has failed.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit contains an aesthetic that reminds one of the films of Wes Anderson, but with far more content and ambitions. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Waititi keeps his distinctive voice in tact with Jojo Rabbit, a poignant anti-war satire that is also his funniest film to date.
reviews.author: Shane Slater

reviews.text: Taika Waititi knocks it out of der park with the meaningful lunacy of his anti-hate satire, which is equal parts Mel Brooks, Wes Anderson and Waititi's own whimsical brilliance.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: The film's central message, that hate arrives not as a monster but as your friend, is movingly depicted.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: No one is here to educate on or avenge for the horrors of the past - it's too silly for that, but it's crystal-clear that Waititi is laughing on the right side of history.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: In its precision, Jojo Rabbit may remind you of Wes Anderson's The Grand Budapest Hotel, another comedy in which clownish forces of fascism squared off against love, humor and elegance -- both movies feel like they come from the same universe.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: It's a tender-hearted film eager to find the saving grace of humor amidst horror. That's to be commended, even if it only partly succeeds.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Waititi has an uncanny ability to find strange interpretations of dire war-torn situations. He's not just making this film for the sheer shock value; Waititi is far too clever for that.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is sweet and whimsical, with an undercurrent of a darker reality...
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is a triumph, a film of brave sophistication and brilliant humor.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: And as good as Davis, McKenzie, Johansson and Sam Rockwell are, it's Waititi who ultimately gives the film's trickiest performance...
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: While the movie and its cast are undoubtedly funny and this film is entertaining, the story lacks depth beyond a couple of silly skits
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Waititi's film is as fun as it is surprising. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel Martínez Mantilla

reviews.text: Waititi shows us the world through a child's eyes so that we understand the power - and the appeal - of jingoism, partisanship, and indoctrination.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: Playing a very risky game...Waititi raises the stakes with every joke he tells...skirting the inappropriate but remaining ever grounded in the savagery of anti-Semitism...and war.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: I love Jojo Rabbit with my whole heart, and it is the perfect blend of Waititi's wit and ability to pack a comedy with an emotional punch-a definite must-see.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is more of a roast than a reckoning, which I suppose would be fine if it were only aiming for comedy. But this is a movie with lofty humanist ideas.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit doesn't quite come together the way its opening promises and, most shockingly, lacks the punch it needs to really work.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Even if I don't love Jojo Rabbit (which is based on a novel by Christine Leunens that I now intend to read), I love that it exists and that Waititi has forced me to reexamine my own responses.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: Neither the masterpiece nor the atrocity it will be described as from here on out by fans and critics alike, Jojo Rabbit is pretty funny, mostly fine, and (perhaps worst of all) well-made.
reviews.author: C.J. Prince

reviews.text: Scarlett Johansson's performance is one of her best in recent memory.
reviews.author: Jason Guerrasio

reviews.text: Disposable frivolity that promises fun at the cinema, if not resonance.
reviews.author: Jane Crowther

reviews.text: [I]f "Jojo Rabbit" has anything to teach us, it's that sniffles can be an even greater divider.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit excels with at least a sincerely attempted - if not exactly precise - balance of humour and horror, absurdity and tragedy.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: While the film is an unashamedly irreverent satire of a painfully relevant moment in modern history, the humour perfectly supplements the true potency of its deeply important message.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: While the film doles out platitudes the adult in us finds overtly simplistic for complicated times... Johansson delightfully surprises with affection and sincerity. Thomasin Mackenzie delivers a defiant rebuttal against Eurocentric exceptionalism...
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: With rising tides of hate and ignorance, where demagogues have groupies and neo-Nazis are easy to find on the internet, preying on the weak, what Jojo Rabbit has to say is both hysterically funny and grim as hell.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Waititi isn't making light of Nazis; he's mocking them, denying them and their present-day analogues the dignity of taking them-as distinct from the very real threat they pose-seriously.
reviews.author: Sam Adams

reviews.text: "Jojo Rabbit" exists in service of a single idea, a notion so desperately idealistic that it lands somewhere between naïveté and disingenuousness.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: Conventional, lazy and incredibly irresponsible filmmaking
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Certainly, JOJO RABBIT won't be to everyone's tastes, but it's a thoughtful, well-intentioned piece of work that often works brilliantly. Some will love it, some will despise it, but hopefully, none will dismiss it.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Yes, Waititi has made a sugary fantasy in the most unlikely places...But in the process, it buries the awful truth.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: What Waititi thinks is shockingly audacious is in fact frustratingly timid, he opts for a gentle prod when maybe a punch would do.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: [Waititi] finds such strange, sweet humor in his storytelling that the movie somehow maintains its ballast, even when the tone inevitably (and it feels, necessarily) shifts.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: There's some sort of strange magic residing in Taika Waititi's Jojo Rabbit, a film that really shouldn't work - but does, with remarkable results.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Waititi is incapable of dealing with the twin horrors of oppression and indoctrination beyond cheap-seats sentimentality and joke-making.
reviews.author: Keith Uhlich

reviews.text: There are brief flashes of something worthwhile - one late scene feels genuinely daring in light of the film's otherwise jovial tone, but it takes so long to get there, it's almost completely lost.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: It's a feel-good movie, all right, but one that uses the fake danger of defanged black comedy to leave us feeling good about the fact that we're above a feel-good movie.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Just as it was easy to like 1999 multiple Oscar winner Life Is Beautiful, it was even easier to dislike it, and the same holds true for Jojo Rabbit...
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: There's a tricky way of addressing the Holocaust and/or World War 2 through satire and humor but Jojo Rabbit does so in a perfect way.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Taika Waititi scores again thanks to his signature style of comedy, excellent cast, and message of love and hope.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: Jojo Rabbit is hilarious with a weighty message that resonates with audiences today and begs us to remember the past.
reviews.author: Ashley Menzel

synopsis: Jojo is a lonely German boy who discovers that his single mother is hiding a Jewish girl in their attic. Aided only by his imaginary friend -- Adolf Hitler -- Jojo must confront his blind nationalism as World War II continues to rage on.
